narrative: Met with Marcus and Elena from Valero Dynamics at their main assembly plant—they run about 4,000 employees across three sites and export roughly 80% of their turbine skids to South America and Europe. They're re-evaluating components for their next production run scheduled for Q4 this year, aiming to replace their incumbent supplier, H-P Controls. Elena mentioned their current setup suffers from frequent drift issues causing costly recalibration visits for their overseas field techs. Right now, we're in technical review with their systems group. Marcus handed the folder to their lead electrical engineer, though he explicitly noted their engineering dept hasn't looked over our pinout and pressure threshold specs yet. Their big hang-up right now is product reliability; Elena stated bluntly that they are worried about membrane fatigue and housing seal failures in high-vibration field environments, citing a bad run with another brand years ago. On a side note, Marcus mentioned the plant cafeteria just switched catering vendors to a taco truck on Thursdays. Target award date remains within the year before their fiscal budget locks in November.
objections: worried about membrane fatigue and housing seal failures
label: request_spec_review
label_rationale: Engineering has not yet checked the pinout and pressure specification, so the fit is open; the reliability worry cannot be tested with a limited first quantity until the specification is confirmed.

narrative: Met with Elena, lead systems engineer at a mid-sized cartoning OEM (~200 staff). They export over 75% of their finished packaging lines to European and Asian pharma clients. Elena was drinking iced tea because the 3rd-floor coffee machine broke down again this morning. They are in the earliest research phase for a new modular frame and have no existing sensor vendor selected for this platform. She stated they are just gathering component options and currently have no plan for purchasing hardware. Their main headache right now on current R&D rigs is excessive wiring bulk slowing down build times. She noted that the machine controller accepts linear position sensors with IO-Link. The customer states that this requirement cannot be changed.
label: nurture
label_rationale: IO-Link is a supported interface of the linear position sensors (pd-009), so the fit is good, but the customer is in early research with no plan to purchase.

hook.requirement: the machine controller accepts linear position sensors with IO-Link

narrative: Dropped by Miller Stamping today, neat little family shop run by 12 people serving local ag builders. Met with Dave in their tooling room. He confirmed the specs on our high-temp proximity sensors match their stamping line requirements 100%. Right now they use sensors from WestTech. Dave said our unit pricing looks way too high compared to what WestTech charges them. Mentioned they have no budget allocated and no plan to purchase any replacements this year anyway since their current stock is full. Also noted their coffee machine was down.
objections: unit pricing looks way too high
label: nurture
label_rationale: Specifications match, but there is no budget, stock is full and no purchase is planned this year; the price remark has no purchase behind it.

narrative: Quick call with Tom from AeroPack, a 15-person outfit assembling custom vacuum packaging rigs. Exports about 85% of their machines to South America. He is in a massive bind and needs to buy 25 digital flow meters immediately for a batch shipping Friday. He currently sources everything from DeltaSense, but their warehouse had severe flooding. He has not checked our spec sheets or pinout diagrams yet to see if our units match, just forwarded their wiring diagram. Mentioned their receptionist brought in homemade donuts.
label: request_spec_review
label_rationale: There is an immediate need for 25 flow meters, but nobody has checked the specification or pinout against the wiring diagram the customer forwarded.

narrative: Met with Dan from Redline Hydraulics at their shop out by the rail yard. Small operation, only about twelve fabricators on the floor and two engineers building custom fluid power units purely for regional lumber mills across the state. They are developing their first electronically regulated rig to stop using manual dial gauges, so there is no previous sensor supplier involved on this platform. Dan's main headache right now is erratic fluid pressure spikes causing burst seals on test benches. We walked through their design layout, but their chief engineer admitted he hasn't checked our sensor spec sheets against their PLC analog input cards yet because he was slammed with a pump recall. Also, Dan complained about the temperature inside their shop because the main HVAC compressor failed yesterday. The project is set for commissioning in nine months, so they plan to issue the purchase order within the year. However, Dan raised a serious issue when I mentioned our standard delivery schedule; he said that 16-week shipping turnaround is unacceptable for their prototype schedule and could blow up their fabrication timeline.
pain_points: erratic fluid pressure spikes causing burst seals
objections: 16-week shipping turnaround is unacceptable
label: request_spec_review
label_rationale: The chief engineer has not checked the sensor specification against the controller input cards; delivery time depends on which variant fits, and the order is planned within the year.

narrative: Cold drop-in with Mark, owner of K-Pack Solutions (around 8 staff building compact syrup filling stations). Nearly all their units ship out to bottlers in Mexico and Chile. He gave me a quick tour of their shop floor—mentioned they just repaved the back loading bay last Friday. Right now they have no incumbent sensor supplier because this filling skid is a brand new ground-up R&D project. Mark admitted they are struggling with inconsistent fill volumes on their mock-up rig and getting erratic baseline readings. However, specs are totally up in the air; his team is debating between electromagnetic flow meters or inline pressure transducers and they don't know what IP rating they'll end up needing. Absolutely no timeline or procurement schedule in place yet; he said purchasing is nowhere on the horizon until engineering figures out the core architecture.
label: nurture
label_rationale: Requirements are undecided and the owner says purchasing is nowhere on the horizon.

narrative: Met with Greg, procurement head at Apex Hydraulics (around 220 staff, supply purely domestic heavy machinery). He confirmed the displacement sensor specs match their new cylinder housing requirements completely. We were going over contract pricing and payment terms for the blanket agreement. Their existing supplier has been in place for six years, but Greg mentioned they suffer from sensor drift during extended runs and frequent recalibration downtime. However, Greg raised an objection stating corporate policy demands a mandatory on-site supplier quality audit before any contract can be executed. He also noted that because of capex freeze reviews, there is no fixed timeline to actually issue POs or start purchasing this fiscal year. Side note, he showed me the new ergonomic desks they just installed throughout purchasing.
objections: mandatory on-site supplier quality audit
label: schedule_site_visit
label_rationale: Specifications are confirmed and corporate policy requires an on-site supplier audit before any contract; the audit can proceed while the order timeline is undecided.

narrative: Spoke with Pete, owner of Kestrel Fluidics, a 12-person outfit handling localized wastewater treatment for municipal car washes across the tri-county area. Purely domestic regional focus, no export business. They have no existing sensor vendor in place; field techs have just been logging pressure off analog dial gauges manually twice a day. That setup failed yesterday when an undetected line surge caused a major tank overflow and halted cleaning operations. Pete said he needs to buy four digital pressure sensors immediately to get everything back online before tomorrow morning. He handed me a folded printout outlining their operating parameters, fluid media, and port dimensions, but I haven't reviewed their technical specs or verified anything against our catalog yet. While we sat in his front office—which smells like fresh paint from their recent remodel—I mentioned our typical list pricing per unit. Pete balked right away, saying our list price is way too steep for a company of his size and would wipe out their remaining maintenance reserve. He asked if there are any immediate price cuts.
objections: list price is way too steep
label: request_spec_review
label_rationale: The customer handed over operating parameters that have not been checked against the catalogue; a price discussion is premature until the fit is known.

narrative: Met with procurement at Heartland Sauces (medium domestic food co, about 180 staff). We're going over contract terms for their new batching setup, which has no existing vendor contracts in place. Their lead engineer reiterated that the process fluid measured by the flow sensor has a viscosity of 6000 millipascal-seconds. He explicitly stated that this requirement cannot be changed. Their plant manager also pointed out their new cafeteria catering service. Regarding the order, they confirmed there is no purchase timeline or scheduled date to sign the deal right now.
label: disqualify
label_rationale: The fixed fluid viscosity of 6,000 mPa.s exceeds the 2,000 mPa.s limit of the flow sensor series (pd-004).

narrative: Met with Dave and the engineering team at Apex Heavy Pipe, one of the biggest domestic structural steel fabricators in the country with zero overseas business. We are in technical review for their furnace exit displacement monitoring project. Their lead tech mentioned their current vendor's units keep failing early, creating excessive downtime on Line 2. narrative: Initial intro call with Marco at Veloce Fluidics, a boutique builder of skid-mounted dosing units with about 18 staff. Target order placement is slated for early Q4 this year, as the skid build is scheduled to start in November. He sent over the engineering drawings and P&ID right after we hung up. label_rationale: The fixed requirement for an independent hygienic design certificate cannot be met for the level sensors (pd-011, pd-017), and the flow meters alone do not make up the instrumentation package.
